description: Turning data into charts and maps that people read correctly: how visual perception works, choosing the right chart for the question, colour, labelling and annotation, plotting with code, interactive web visualisation, geographic data and maps, and telling an honest story with data. Every chart is built in code in the browser, critiqued against perception principles and redesigned until it works on a small phone screen as well as a projector.
modelledOn: Tufte, The Visual Display of Quantitative Information
Cairo, How Charts Lie: Getting Smarter about Visual Information
outcomes: Explain how preattentive features, visual channels and Gestalt principles determine what a reader sees in a chart.
Choose and justify a chart type from the data types and the question being asked.
Apply colour, labelling and annotation that are accessible, colour-blind safe and honest.
Build static and interactive visualisations in code with a grammar-of-graphics library and web technologies.
Map geographic data correctly with appropriate projections, choropleths and symbol maps.
Design a data story for a stated audience and identify and correct misleading charts.

units.title: Why visualise and the data behind a chart
topics: Exploration versus explanation; Anscombe's quartet and the Datasaurus dozen
Data types: nominal, ordinal, interval, ratio, temporal and spatial; tidy data and long versus wide formats
Munzner's what, why and how framework: data abstraction, task abstraction and idioms
A short history: Playfair, Nightingale, Minard, Snow and Tukey

units.title: Principles of visual perception
topics: Preattentive processing and pop-out; visual search
Marks and channels; the ranking of channels for quantitative and categorical data (Cleveland and McGill, Mackinlay)
Gestalt principles: proximity, similarity, enclosure, connection, continuity and closure
Weber's law, area and angle judgement errors; why 3D and pie charts mislead
Change blindness, working memory limits and the data-ink ratio

units.title: Choosing the right chart
topics: Comparing categories: bar, dot and lollipop charts; ordering and baselines
Distributions: histograms and bin width, density plots, box plots, violin and strip plots
Relationships: scatter plots, overplotting remedies, bubble charts, scatter-plot matrices and correlation heatmaps
Change over time: line charts, slope charts, area charts, and when to use a log scale
Part-to-whole and hierarchy: stacked bars, treemaps, sunbursts and Sankey diagrams for flows
Small multiples and faceting; multivariate views and parallel coordinates
Matching a chart to a question about mobile money transaction volumes by region

units.title: Colour, labels and annotation
topics: Colour models: RGB, HSL and perceptually uniform spaces such as CIELAB and OKLCH
Sequential, diverging and qualitative palettes; why the rainbow scale misleads
Colour-vision deficiency, contrast ratios and accessible chart design
Titles that state the finding, direct labelling instead of legends, axis and tick choices
Annotation layers: highlighting, reference lines, callouts and uncertainty bands

units.title: Plotting with code
topics: The grammar of graphics: data, aesthetics, geometries, scales, coordinates, facets and themes
Plotting in Python with Matplotlib, seaborn and a declarative library such as Vega-Lite or Altair
Data wrangling for charts with pandas: reshaping, grouping, aggregating and joining
Visualising uncertainty: error bars, confidence bands, quantile dot plots and hypothetical outcome plots
Reproducible figures: scripts, themes, export formats (SVG, PNG) and resolution
Exploring cocoa export and price data from raw tables to a publication-quality figure

units.title: Interactive and web-based visualisation
topics: SVG, Canvas and WebGL as rendering targets; performance with large data
D3.js fundamentals: selections, data joins, scales, axes and transitions
Interaction techniques: tooltips, filtering, brushing and linking, zooming, details on demand (Shneiderman's mantra)
Responsive and mobile-first charts; keyboard access and screen-reader descriptions
Designing for low-bandwidth users: small payloads, server-side aggregation and progressive loading
Building a linked dashboard of district health indicators that works on a basic smartphone

units.title: Maps and geographic data
topics: Coordinate reference systems, latitude and longitude, map projections and their distortions
Geographic data formats: GeoJSON, TopoJSON and shapefiles; joining attribute data to boundaries
Choropleth maps: normalisation by population or area, classification schemes and the modifiable areal unit problem
Symbol, dot-density and flow maps; cartograms and hexagonal tile maps
Web maps with tiles and a library such as Leaflet; simplifying geometries for small downloads
Mapping rainfall across northern Ghana and access to health facilities by district

units.title: Data storytelling and avoiding misleading charts
topics: Narrative structures: martini glass, drill-down and scrollytelling; knowing the audience
From exploration to explanation: choosing the one message and removing clutter
Misleading techniques: truncated and dual axes, cherry-picked ranges, area distortion, hidden denominators
Ethics of visualisation: representing people, uncertainty and missing data honestly
Critique and redesign of published charts from news and government reports
Capstone: a data story on a Ghanaian or African dataset, with code, peer critique and a redesign

schedule.title: Why we visualise
schedule.exercise: Compare the summary statistics of the Anscombe datasets, then explain in a paragraph what only the plots reveal. Read one historical chart and say what question it answered.

tasks.title: Plot the four Anscombe datasets as scatter plots with fitted lines and print their identical means, variances and correlations alongside
Reshape a wide table of monthly cocoa prices by region into tidy long format and verify row counts and column types
Take three published charts and write each one's what, why and how analysis, then rebuild one as code using a different idiom

schedule.title: Perception and visual encoding
schedule.exercise: Rank the encodings position, length, angle, area and colour for a quantitative variable and justify using the perception studies. Mark the data-ink in a cluttered chart.

tasks.title: Encode the same five regional values as bars, circles of area and angles in a pie, and note which is hardest to compare
Build a pop-out test with one red dot among 50 blue dots and one with a mixed shape condition, then compare the search times
Redesign a cluttered 3D chart by removing chart junk, applying Gestalt grouping and raising the data-ink ratio, then explain each change

schedule.title: Core chart types
schedule.exercise: For six given questions, choose the best chart type and say what you would avoid. Explain the effect of bin width on a histogram of farm yields.

tasks.title: Plot a sorted horizontal bar chart of export tonnes by crop with a zero baseline and direct value labels
Show a distribution of 500 household incomes with histograms at three bin widths and a box and violin plot, then compare readings
Plot 100000 mobile money transactions as a scatter, fix the overplotting with transparency, binning or hexbins, and compare the readability of each

schedule.title: Composition, small multiples and question matching
schedule.exercise: Write down five questions about mobile money volumes by region and match each to a chart type with a one-line reason.

tasks.title: Show the share of mobile money volume by region with a stacked bar and a treemap and say which one reads better
Facet monthly transaction volume into small multiples for 16 districts with shared axes and sort panels by total volume
Query transaction volumes by region and month with SQL, then choose and build three charts that answer distinct stakeholder questions

schedule.title: Colour, labels and annotation
schedule.exercise: Evaluate a rainbow-coloured map for colour-vision accessibility and write a replacement palette recommendation with contrast ratios.

tasks.title: Draw one heatmap with a rainbow scale and one with a perceptually uniform sequential scale, and list what the rainbow hides
Simulate deuteranopia on a six-colour chart, compute contrast ratios against the background and replace failing colours with accessible ones
Turn a default line chart into an annotated chart with finding title, direct labels, a reference line and a shaded uncertainty band

schedule.title: Grammar of graphics and wrangling
schedule.exercise: Describe a given chart as data, aesthetics, geometry, scale, coordinate and facet layers, then say which layer to change to answer a new question.

tasks.title: Build the same scatter plot of rainfall and yield with a declarative library by mapping x, y, colour and size aesthetics
Use pandas to join, group and pivot two district tables and produce a tidy frame ready for a faceted chart, checking row counts
Reproduce one published chart three ways in Matplotlib, a declarative library and a statistical wrapper, comparing code length and flexibility

schedule.title: Uncertainty and reproducible figures
schedule.exercise: Describe how a reader may misread a bar chart with standard error bars and propose a clearer way to show the same estimate.

tasks.title: Add 95 percent confidence intervals to a bar chart of mean cocoa price by year and state what overlapping intervals imply
Write a script that regenerates a figure from raw data and exports SVG and PNG at 300 dpi with a consistent theme
Clean a raw cocoa export and price table and produce a publication-quality figure with uncertainty, annotations and a caption stating the main finding

schedule.title: Web graphics and interaction
schedule.exercise: Decide whether SVG or Canvas suits a chart of 200 points and a chart of 200000 points, and justify with expected rendering cost.

tasks.title: Use D3-style selections and a data join to draw ten bars from an array with scales and axes, and update them with new data
Add tooltips and a region filter to a scatter plot so hovering shows details and the filter dims unselected points
Render the same 100000 point scatter in SVG and Canvas, measure frame time while zooming and recommend a rendering approach

schedule.title: Dashboards for low-bandwidth users
schedule.exercise: Write a payload budget for a district health dashboard on a 2G connection and list what you will cut to meet it.

tasks.title: Make a bar chart responsive so it reflows at 360 pixels wide and add a text description and keyboard focus order for screen readers
Aggregate 1 million health visit rows to monthly district totals in SQL and report how much the chart payload shrinks
Build a linked dashboard of district health indicators where selecting a district updates three charts, within a 150 KB total payload

schedule.title: Geographic data and choropleths
schedule.exercise: Explain why Mercator inflates Greenland and which projection you would pick for a map of Ghana, with a reason.

tasks.title: Plot the outline of Ghana in three map projections and compare the area distortion visible in each
Join district health counts to a GeoJSON boundary file by district code, report unmatched names and fix them
Map malaria cases per district as raw counts and as rates per 1000 with equal-interval and quantile classes, and explain how the story changes

schedule.title: More map types and web maps
schedule.exercise: For a flow of cocoa from districts to ports, argue whether a flow map, symbol map or cartogram best shows the pattern.

tasks.title: Draw a proportional symbol map of cocoa output for 10 districts and add a legend that shows three reference sizes
Simplify district boundaries at three tolerances, compare file size and visual fidelity, and pick the best tolerance for a mobile map
Map rainfall across northern Ghana with a layered web map and add health facility catchments showing districts more than 10 km from a clinic

schedule.title: Storytelling and misleading charts
schedule.exercise: Pick a misleading chart from the news, list the techniques it uses and write the honest version's title and axis choices.

tasks.title: Plot the same data with a truncated and a zero-based axis and measure how much the apparent difference grows
Take an exploratory chart of food prices, pick one message and rework it with a clear title, muted context and a single highlight
Build a scrollytelling sequence of four views for a school enrolment dataset that follows a martini-glass structure and ends in open exploration

schedule.title: Ethics, critique and capstone
schedule.exercise: Swap capstone drafts with a peer and write a structured critique covering message, encoding, honesty and accessibility.

tasks.title: Show a dataset with missing values in a chart by marking gaps visibly, then compare to silently dropping the rows and explain the risk
Critique a government report chart against a checklist and redraw it with corrected axes, labels and colour, noting each change
Produce a data story on an African dataset with at least four coordinated figures, runnable code, a peer critique log and a redesign
